summary: All five requirements are met and verified. The controller returns HTTP 422 with reason RANGE_BEFORE_START and earliestBillingPeriod only for the readable-but-out-of-coverage price-vs-volume case (resolve empty + coverage.reason()==RANGE_BEFORE_START), while every other empty reason still returns 409 via noCurSource and the missing-quantity cannotAnswer 422 path is untouched. The frontend fetchPriceVsVolume stops collapsing non-OK to null, returning a PriceVolumeCoverageGap on the coverage 422 and null for 409/502/wrong-shape; PriceVsVolumeSection renders the coverage-specific sentence (not the generic usage-quantity banner, which is kept only for true null), preserves the empty-array message, and comparisonOptions(earliest) offers only answerable pairs defaulting to the newest covered one on the AWS-default path. product_product_name is guarded via serviceNameColumn (CurColumnCatalog) with a product_servicecode fallback at every SQL call site in both CurAdvancedMetricsService and CurCostDataSource, with product_product_name still the default; no unguarded literals remain outside the helper and Javadoc. Split math and the line_item_usage_amount query are byte-identical. Backend targeted tests pass (CurInsightsControllerTest 36, CurCostDataSourceTest 17, CurAdvancedMetricsServiceTest 56; 109 total, 0 failures), frontend npm run build (tsc+vite) passes, and the only frontend test failures (7) are a pre-existing localStorage.setItem ThemeContext stub issue that reproduces identically on the unmodified main checkout and is unrelated to this change.
